cor.heading: Cost of Revenues
cor.text: Factorial is a development stage company and is in the early stages of commercializing our technology. Factorial expects the majority of the costs of revenues will initially be driven by labor, overhead, logistics, and direct material expenses related to the production of cells as well as costs incurred in excess of the NRV of certain inventory.

opex.text: Based on its current operating plan, the Company estimates that its cash and cash equivalents as of the date of this filing will be sufficient to fund its operating expenses and capital expenditure requirements into the first half of 2028. The Company has based this estimate on assumptions that may prove to be wrong and could deplete its liquid resources sooner than it currently expects.

The Company has based this estimate on assumptions that may prove to be wrong and could deplete its liquid resources sooner than it currently expects.

rd.heading: Research and Development
rd.text:
Research and development expenses decreased by $1.8 million, or 30.8%, for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025. The decline primarily resulted from $2.6 million of expense reimbursements from joint development partners, offset by an increase of $0.8 million of payroll and benefit costs, for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025.

Research and development expenses decreased by $6.8 million, or 35.0%, for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The decline primarily resulted from the recognition of $6.2 million of expense reimbursements from joint development partners for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to $0.3 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, as well as lower facility costs from the exit of our Methuen facility in October 2025.

sm.text: General and administrative expenses consist mainly of personnel-related expenses for Factorial’s executive, sales and marketing and other administrative functions and expenses for outside professional services, including legal, accounting and other advisory services. Factorial is expanding its headcount in anticipation of planning for and ramping up commercial manufacturing operations and to meet public company financial and compliance requirements. Accordingly, in addition to the non-recurring transaction costs discussed above, Factorial expects its general and administrative expenses to increase significantly in the near term and for the foreseeable future.

ga.heading: General and Administrative
ga.text: General and administrative expenses increased by $1.9 million, or 42.3%, for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025, primarily driven by an increase in professional fees, including legal, audit, investment banking, and advisory services. This was offset by a $1.0 million decrease in stock-based compensation expense.

nonop.heading: Other Income, Net
nonop.text:
Other income, net increased by $1.4 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025, primarily due to fluctuations in the effects of foreign exchange offset by interest incurred on the legal judgment.

Other income, net increased by $0.6 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the nine months ended September 30, 2025, due to fluctuations in the effects of foreign exchange offset by a reduction of interest income.

tax.heading: Provision for Income Taxes
tax.text: Factorial’s income tax provision consists of an estimate for U.S. federal and state income taxes based on enacted rates, as adjusted for allowable credits, deductions, uncertain tax positions, changes in deferred tax assets and liabilities, and changes in the tax law. Factorial maintains a valuation allowance against the full value of its U.S. and state net deferred tax assets because Factorial believes the recoverability of the tax assets is not more likely than not.

ocf.text: Factorial’s cash flows used in operating activities to date have been primarily comprised of payroll, material and supplies, facilities expense, inventory purchases, and professional services related to research and development and general and administrative activities. wc.text: Factorial expects its capital expenditures and working capital requirements to increase materially in the near future, as it seeks to accelerate its research and development efforts and scale up the production operations with its OEM partners. Factorial expects to satisfy early demand for its solid-state battery products by expanding its existing fabrication line operations in South Korea and the United States, to support initial commercial production. During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, Factorial paid capital expenditures for such expansion of approximately $3.4 million and expects to incur a total of capital expenditures in a range of $10.0 million to $12.0 million for the fiscal year ending 2026. The expansion is expected to be completed in phases by 2028. Beyond the initial investment to expand our existing fabrication line operations in South Korea and the United States, we do not plan to build or acquire additional manufacturing facilities or incur substantial capital expenditures for the expansion of our existing facilities. Instead, as demand grows, including incremental high spec applications and gigawatt-scale ramp-up in the automotive market, we expect to scale primarily through a partner manufacturing approach.

capex.text: Factorial’s cash flows used in investing activities, to date, have been comprised of purchases of property and equipment and purchases and disposals of equipment. Factorial expects the costs to acquire property and equipment to increase in the near future as it builds pilot and sample production lines for its FEST Silicon and Solstice programs.

net sales.heading: Revenues
net sales.text: To date, Factorial has produced revenue through the production and delivery of cells to customers in the aerospace industry.

intro.text: We are a blank check company incorporated on October 29, 2024 as a Cayman Islands exempted company and formed for the purpose of effecting a merger, amalgamation, share exchange, asset acquisition, share purchase, or reorganization or engaging in any other similar business combination with one or more businesses or entities, which we refer to throughout this Annual Report as our initial business combination. While we may pursue our initial business combination in any business industry or sector, we have initially focused on seeking high-growth businesses with proven or potential transnational operations or outlooks in order to capitalize on the experience, reputation, and network of our management team.

s.t: ◦ The conversion of each issued and outstanding share of Series A-1, Series A-2, Series B-1, Series C-1, Series C-2, and Series D redeemable convertible preferred stock (together the “Legacy Factorial Preferred Stock”) into a number of shares of Legacy Factorial Common Stock in accordance with the terms of Section 5.1 of the Factorial Certificate of Incorporation in effect immediately prior to the Merger Effective Time; and
(iii) an aggregate of 67,314,957 shares of Series A Common Stock issued to holders of Legacy Factorial Preferred Stock from the exchange of shares of Legacy Factorial Preferred Stock;

(iv) an aggregate of 2,811,447 shares of Series A Common Stock issued to holders of the Legacy Factorial Convertible Notes from conversion of the Legacy Factorial Convertible Notes along with accrued interest into shares of Legacy Factorial Common Stock immediately before the Merger and the subsequent exchange into shares of Series A Common Stock; and (v) an aggregate of 362,625 shares of Series A Common Stock issued to holders of the Legacy Factorial Warrants from their cashless exercise of the warrants for shares of Legacy Factorial Preferred Stock and converted into shares of Legacy Factorial Common Stock immediately before the Merger and subsequent exchange for Series A Common Stock.

Immediately prior to the closing of the Merger, all outstanding shares of Preferred Stock automatically converted into an equivalent number of shares of Legacy Factorial common stock on a one -to-one basis.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Other receivables
lines.why: Owed by suppliers and others, not by customers (vendor non-trade receivables): operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
